subject: BrightLoop onboarding: index population & rerank validation sprint

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLoop onboarding: index population & rerank validation sprint

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Per our conversation, this thread is to kick off the implementation playbook for the embeddings -> rerank migration and the index population sprint. I’ve attached an initial timeline and a short index-backfill checklist for your engineering and data teams.

High-level goals for the sprint (2 weeks):
- Bring the existing catalog (1.2M docs) into the vector store with seed priming for top-50 queries.
- Run rerank evals across a 200-sample prompt set and produce quality baselines.
- Validate cold-start latency and fallback behavior for the SaaS search endpoint.

Immediate asks from BrightLoop:
1) Confirm your preferred vector DB (we support Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate, and self-hosted FAISS).
2) Share an S3 path or a temporary read-only DB credential with export samples (first 50 records) so we can sanity-check schema/encoding.
3) Set up a 1-hour sync with your data engineers (suggested: Fri 4/9 10:00am PT).

Attachments: implementation_timeline_v1.xlsx (xlsx), index_backfill_checklist.md (md)

Next steps — internal: I’m looping Karthik to propose the technical plan and Marissa for CSM milestones and success criteria. Ben will coordinate the dev resources for the backfill.

Thanks,
Olga
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

- Data access: I uploaded a 50-record sample to s3://brightloop-onboarding/samples/sample_50.json (read-only key shared separately).
- Sync: Fri 4/9 10:00am PT works for Devon and me.

Two logistics notes from procurement: we’ll need a short statement on data residency (we operate in US cloud regions only) and a draft SOW for the backfill work before the 4/16 kickoff. Procurement included a stub email for the SOW request.

Emily / Olga —

Thanks for the sample and the quick responses. A few technical clarifications and proposed checklist items before the sync:

1) Vector DB approach
- If BrightLoop chooses Milvus for production, we recommend a staged approach: (a) Pinecone sandbox for the POC to speed iteration, (b) Milvus staging cluster for scale tests, (c) final cutover to Milvus prod.

2) Index backfill considerations (notes we’ll present Friday):
- Sharding strategy: suggest document sharding by tenant_id (tenant keyed) to support parallel backfills.
- Metadata preservation: preserve source url, last_updated, and category tags. We’ll supply a small ingestion shim to map fields.
- Batch size and throttle: begin with 500-doc batches for the first 10k docs, then increase to 5k after warmup monitoring.

3) Rerank eval plan (quick outline)
- Use the 200-sample prompt set from your analytics team + 100 adversarial queries we’ll add.
- Metric set: NDCG@10, MRR, precision@5, and human-labeled pass/fail for the top 3 results.
- Baseline: current BrightLoop ranking model output; Goal: >= 12% improvement in NDCG@10 for top use cases or acceptable degradation with cost improvements.

I’ve attached a skeletal rerank eval prompts file (rerank_evals_sample_prompts.jsonl) and a short index_backfill_checklist.md to the calendar invite for reference. For the Friday meeting I’ll present a staged backfill timeline and failure-handling runbook.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Emily —

Thanks for confirming the sync. I’ve scheduled Fri 4/9 10:00am PT (30m) and attached the meeting agenda. Primary success criteria we want to agree on in the call:
- Index completeness target: 95% of production catalog in vector store within sprint window.
- Acceptable latency envelope: 90th percentile query latency < 220ms for seeded queries.
- Rerank acceptance: pass human review for at least 160/200 samples or documented rationale tied to retrieval failures.

Pre-call ask for BrightLoop engineers: please have one engineer with access to the S3 samples and one engineer who can speak to the current ranking logs.

I’ll also upload a draft SOW for the backfill work to the shared Drive after the call; procurement can use that as a starting point.

Best,
